ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: What part of the eye is between C and B in the figure shown here?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is a cross-section diagram of an eye. Label C is placed inside the large central/back chamber of the eyeball, while label B is near the front upper outer region. Between the front region near B and the central region near C, the diagram shows the front optical opening associated with the iris, in front of the lens. Reasoning: In eye anatomy, the opening in the iris that lets light enter and lies in front of the lens is called the pupil. Therefore, the part of the eye between C and B is the pupil.
